correctness.rationale: With both edges oriented from the same part, the shortest distances conditional on same, incident, or disjoint labels have laws |U−V|, U+V, and 2−|U−V|. For incident edges sharing their first endpoint, the alternate cross routes exceed x+y by 2−2x or 2−2y, and the opposite-endpoint route has length 4−x−y; the other orientation is reflected. For disjoint edges the two cross routes have lengths 2±(x−y), while the same-part routes have lengths at least two. The per-edge label counts 1, N−2, P−N+1 give the stated mixture and both CDF branches, including the single-edge and four-cycle cases. At fixed N the difference is the positive factor 1/Psmall−1/Plarge times B_N. B_N is strictly positive in the interior; on [1,2] its quadratic in u=2−t has maximum 2(N−1)^2/(3N−4), and the density difference is positive up to that threshold and negative after it, so TV (supremum over measurable sets) equals the threshold gap. The three component first moments 1/3, 1, 5/3 give the W1 constant via stochastic order and quantile coupling; the second moments 1/6, 7/6, 17/6 give the stated second moment. The star and balanced mixture weights give the stated limits. This is a proof for unit lengths and independent normalized arclength, not vertex sampling or an unequal-length network.
